subject: sunflower sea star
title: The Fastest Starfish Has 24 Arms, and 90% of Them Died in Five Years

scenes.text: A starfish with 24 arms, a metre across, moving a metre a minute. Then it nearly vanished.
The sunflower sea star, Alaska to southern California. The heaviest starfish alive, about five kilos, on 15,000 tube feet.
It's the fastest starfish on record, a metre a minute, and one of the main predators of sea urchins.
In 2013, a wasting disease began killing sea stars from Mexico to Alaska. This species lost around 90 percent in five years. Near Washington state, 99 percent.
Without them, urchins exploded and ate about 95 percent of Northern California's kelp forests within a decade.
The killer stayed unknown until 2025: a bacterium, Vibrio pectenicida, hiding in the fluid around the organs. Now scientists hope to breed the survivors.

description:
The sunflower sea star has 16 to 24 arms, spans up to a metre, weighs about 5 kg and is the fastest starfish on record at about 1 metre per minute. Since 2013 a wasting disease has wiped out around 90 percent of them.
The disease killed sea stars from Mexico to Alaska and hit this species hardest: about 90 percent lost in the outbreak's first five years, and 99.2 percent near Washington state. It was listed as critically endangered by the IUCN in 2020. With its main predator gone, sea urchins boomed and ate about 95 percent of Northern California's kelp forests within a decade. In 2025 researchers at the Hakai Institute and colleagues identified the bacterium Vibrio pectenicida as a cause (Nature Ecology and Evolution), raising hopes of breeding resistant survivors.
Should we try to bring the kelp forests back?
first_comment: Lose one starfish, lose 95 percent of a kelp forest. Which animal do you think holds up its whole ecosystem?
